page: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is provided via a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2202.0 and high single-threaded throughput in gzip compression at 34.39 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.52 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4320.55 and PassMark memory score of 1708.01 fall into the bottom 25% of tested configurations. Large block uncached memory read and write bandwidths perform in the average range at 41.59 GB/sec and 31.72 GB/sec respectively.

The instance is equipped with advanced CPU instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning and cryptography. While prompt processing for a small 135M LLM model reaches an average speed of 517.73 tokens/sec, text generation for a medium 7B model drops to a poor 4.81 tokens/sec due to the 8.0 GB memory constraint. This hardware profile is suited for single-threaded compute tasks, static web serving, and lightweight database operations utilizing the local NVMe storage, but is constrained for memory-intensive or highly parallelized multi-core workloads.
